summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 30.41% YoY with 46% operating margin; FY26 revenue reached INR149.40 crores, and management reiterated a ~35% revenue CAGR.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue growth of 30.41% YoY, operating profit up nearly 54% at a 46% operating margin, and net profit of INR5.14 crores (up 25.88% YoY, 17.41% margin). FY26 revenue was INR149.40 crores, up about 48% reported and about 20% after adjusting for a one-time INR25.74 crore sale in FY25 from a change in operating method. The company ended FY26 with about INR78 crores of liquid balance, zero debt, and 126 points of sale after adding 32 stores in the year (18 in Q4). Management kept its ~35% revenue CAGR guidance and said at least 20 new stores are planned for FY27.

segments.name: PNGS Gargi SIS (in PNGS Gargi Stores / P.N. Gadgil & Sons)
segments.commentary: 34 SIS points as of FY26; management said SIS SSSG is around 30-32% and that PNGS SIS is about 75-80% of revenue currently. Dependence targeted to fall to about 65% by FY28.

segments.name: EBOs (exclusive brand outlets, FOCO)
segments.commentary: 38 EBOs at FY26 end versus 0 in FY22; management expects EBO growth to drive most incremental revenue. Breakeven is 6-9 months in Maharashtra and 15-18 months outside Maharashtra.

segments.name: Shoppers Stop and other third-party SIS
segments.commentary: 54 third-party SIS points at FY26 end versus 0 in FY22; management said Shoppers Stop expansion is passive and follows its new store openings.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: 14KT studded diamond jewellery is about 35% of revenue (HI colour diamonds). Silver jewellery is 92.5% sterling silver with CZ stones and IGI-certified natural diamonds.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR of approximately 35% over the next few years, maintained; management said FY27 revenue would be about INR190 crores and FY28 about INR260 crores.
At least 20 new stores in FY27; management said it is not capping the count and has cash to fund at least 25 more EBOs without debt or equity.
EBITDA margin expected to stay in the same range in FY27-FY28, with 100-150 bps upside if earlier stores mature faster.
PAT margin of about 20% expected to hold in the near term; management hopes for higher over time.
Marketing spend is about 4-5% of revenue; no change in the expense outlook was given.
capex_capacity: Per-store capex for a FOCO franchise is about INR30-50 lakh for fit-out and premises; total with silver and diamond inventory deposits is about INR80 lakh to INR1 crore. COCO economics are similar.

Breakeven for new stores outside Maharashtra is 15-18 months; within Maharashtra it is 6-9 months. Contribution from outside-Maharashtra stores starts within 8-12 months and inside Maharashtra within 4-6 months.
Maharashtra store count rose from 47 (Mar 2024) to 67 (Mar 2026); management sees room for 8-10 more EBOs in Pune alone.
Store roll-out is about 53% in Maharashtra and about 47% outside, per management. Focus is on north India, with South entry (Hyderabad started; Chennai and Bangalore being evaluated).
Local karigar manufacturing is replacing imports of ready silver jewellery after a government ban on imports; company buys raw silver for in-house making.
demand_pricing: Management said price changes are made only when silver moves by about INR30,000-40,000/kg, given MRP-based pricing and no per-gram pricing; it said a 30% rise in precious metal prices would not materially hit margins.
Management cited double-digit industry growth and low organised-sector penetration; it said millennials and Gen Z are driving demand for lightweight, personalised everyday jewellery.
Management said the South is an early-stage test and it will comment after 4-5 stand-alone South stores by next year-end.
Customer retention runs through discount schemes (monsoon, anniversary, Diwali, Valentine's, year-end), telecalling and WhatsApp CRM.

qa_highlights.question: How will the 35% growth split across PNGS SIS, EBOs and Shoppers Stop in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue would be about INR190 crores and FY28 about INR260 crores. Management expects the PNGS SIS share to fall to about 65% by FY28 from about 78%, with EBOs and other channels making up the rest.

qa_highlights.question: What are the EBO/SIS capex and FOCO economics?
qa_highlights.answer: FOCO franchise capex is about INR30-50 lakh for fit-out and rent, and about INR80 lakh to INR1 crore including inventory deposits. The PNGS SIS sells at markdown and is paid within 2-3 weeks; Shoppers Stop remits monthly.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold as more stores are added and the mix shifts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects PAT margin of about 20% to hold for now. New stores weigh on profit until about 300 locations, after which only about 8-9% of stores are new each year. EBITDA margin should stay in the same range, with 100-150 bps upside.

qa_highlights.question: Could growth exceed 35% and can the company fund growth without new equity?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth could exceed 35% if new EBOs reach maturity faster than the 15-18 month breakeven outside Maharashtra. Management said no equity is needed for organic growth; acquisitions could change that.

qa_highlights.question: How do gold and silver price spikes affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices are adjusted only when silver moves by INR30,000-40,000/kg, and a 30% precious metal rise would not significantly affect margins because of the cushion built in.

qa_highlights.question: Why were store additions accelerated to 32 in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it added more stores because good locations became available, and with its cash it can set up at least 25 FOCO stores without debt or equity.

risks_watch: Growth depends on new EBOs, especially outside Maharashtra, reaching breakeven in 15-18 months; slower maturity would pressure the 35% CAGR.
PNGS SIS dependence is still about 75-80% of revenue, and SIS expansion depends on the parent's own store openings.
Precious metal price volatility; the FOCO/MRP pricing model absorbs moves only above a threshold.
Rising other expenses and marketing (4-5% of revenue) and new-store drag on margins.
The FY26 growth (~48%) is flattered by a one-time INR25.74 crore FY25 sale; underlying growth is about 20%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and cash position, with management repeatedly saying it is conservative in guidance. It was evasive on the segment-wise breakdown of store-level economics and on specific marketing and acquisition plans.
